models.description:
This is a Linear Regression model that predicts the resale price (AskPrice) of used cars in the Indian market based on vehicle attributes: brand, model, age, kilometers driven, transmission type, ownership history, and fuel type. It uses a scikit-learn Pipeline combining OneHotEncoder (for categorical features) and LinearRegression, trained on a cleaned dataset of ~14,500 used car listings.
Usage

Input shape: 1 row × 8 columns (Brand, model, Year,Age, kmDriven, Transmission, Owner, FuelType)
Output shape: 1 float value — predicted AskPrice in ₹
Known/preventable failures:

Predicts poorly on brand/model combinations not seen during training (mitigated with handle_unknown='ignore' in the encoder, which returns a degraded but non-crashing estimate)
Struggles with luxury/exotic cars since they were removed as outliers during cleaning
Linear Regression assumes roughly linear price depreciation — real depreciation is non-linear (steep early years, flattens later), so predictions may be less accurate at extremes of Age

System
Standalone model — not part of a larger pipeline. Takes structured tabular input (7 fields as above) and outputs a single numeric price prediction. No downstream dependencies; output is meant for direct human interpretation (e.g., displaying an estimated price on a used-car listing app).
Implementation requirements
Trained on CPU (no GPU required) — training a Linear Regression model on ~14,500 rows takes seconds. Inference is near-instant (<10ms per prediction). Built with Python, pandas, scikit-learn.

Model Characteristics
Model initialization
Trained from scratch — not fine-tuned from any pre-trained model. Linear Regression is a simple parametric model fit directly on this dataset.
Model stats
Lightweight — the .pkl file is typically under a few hundred KB. No layers/weights in the deep-learning sense; it's a linear coefficient per one-hot-encoded category plus numeric features (Age, kmDriven). Inference latency is negligible (single matrix multiplication).
Other details
Not pruned or quantized (not applicable to Linear Regression). No differential privacy techniques applied — dataset does not contain personally identifiable information about individuals (only vehicle listing data).

Data Overview
Training data
~14,993 used car listings scraped/sourced with columns: Brand, model, Year, Age, kmDriven, Transmission, Owner, FuelType, PostedDate, AdditionInfo, AskPrice.
Preprocessing performed:

Removed rows with missing kmDriven values
Converted kmDriven from string to numeric (handled decimal-formatted strings)
Converted AskPrice from currency-formatted strings (e.g., '₹ 1,95,000') to integers
Removed outlier rows: Year < 1980, and top 1% outliers in kmDriven and AskPrice
Dropped PostedDate and AdditionInfo (not predictive of car value)
Dropped Year in favor of Age (perfectly correlated, redundant)
One-hot encoded categorical columns: Brand, model, Transmission, Owner, FuelType

Final cleaned dataset: ~14,589 rows.
Demographic groups
Not applicable — this dataset contains vehicle listing attributes only (no data about individual buyers/sellers' demographic characteristics).
Evaluation data
80/20 train-test split (random_state=42), with 5-fold cross-validation performed on the training set for a more robust performance estimate.

Evaluation Results
Summary
(Fill in your actual numbers here once you run Step 6/7 from earlier — R² score, MAE, and mean CV R².)
Subgroup evaluation results
No formal subgroup analysis was performed. A reasonable follow-up would be evaluating prediction error separately by Brand or FuelType, since luxury brands or less common fuel types (e.g. Hybrid/CNG) may have fewer training examples and higher error.
Fairness
Not formally assessed. Since this model predicts vehicle prices (not decisions about people), traditional fairness metrics (e.g. demographic parity) don't directly apply. However, if brand/model representation in the training data is imbalanced, predictions for underrepresented brands may be less reliable.
Usage limitations

Not intended for high-stakes financial decisions without human review — treat as an estimate, not an appraisal
Performance will degrade over time as market prices shift (model reflects prices at time of data collection, not real-time market trends)
Not validated on cars outside the Indian used-car market
Not suitable for luxury/exotic vehicles since they were excluded as outliers during training

Ethics
The model could be misused to systematically undervalue certain sellers' listings if deployed without transparency. Users should be informed that predictions are estimates based on historical listing data, not appraisals, and that the underlying data may reflect regional or brand-based pricing biases present in the original listings. No sensitive personal data was used in training.

instances.overview:
# House Price Prediction using Artificial Neural Network (ANN)

## Overview

This deep learning model predicts house prices using property features such as bedrooms, bathrooms, living area, lot size, and number of floors. The model is implemented using TensorFlow/Keras and demonstrates regression with an Artificial Neural Network (ANN).

---

## Deep Learning Architecture

- Input Layer
- Hidden Dense Layer(s)
- ReLU Activation
- Output Layer
- Linear Activation (Regression)

---

## Input Features

- bedrooms
- bathrooms
- sqft_living
- sqft_lot
- floors

---

## Output

Predicted House Price

---

## Technologies Used

- Python
- TensorFlow
- Keras
- Pandas
- NumPy
- Scikit-Learn

---

## Workflow

1. Load Dataset
2. Feature Selection
3. Train-Test Split
4. Feature Scaling
5. Build ANN Regression Model
6. Train the Model
7. Evaluate Performance
8. Predict House Prices

---

## Evaluation Metrics

- Mean Absolute Error (MAE)
- Mean Squared Error (MSE)
- Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE)
- R² Score

---

## Intended Use

This model is designed for educational purposes, demonstrating how deep learning can be applied to house price prediction and regression problems.

---

## Limitations

- Trained on a single housing dataset.
- Uses a limited set of property features.
- Intended for learning and experimentation rather than real-world property valuation.
